name: System
functionality: Hosts kernel threads, drivers, and hardware interrupts.
troubleshooting: High CPU in 'System' usually means a driver problem: use Resource Monitor or Windows Performance Recorder to find the driver.
Update chipset, storage, network, and GPU drivers.
Check for failing disks (I/O retries show up as System CPU).
highCpu: Driver activity: network, storage, or GPU drivers busy or misbehaving; also hardware interrupts from failing devices.

name: Registry
troubleshooting: Normal; memory use reflects registry size.

name: Memory Compression
description: Stores compressed memory pages to avoid paging to disk.
functionality: Stores compressed memory pages to avoid paging to disk.
troubleshooting: High memory here is a symptom of memory pressure, not a problem in itself.
highMemory: Normal when RAM is full — it is compressing other apps' memory. Add RAM or close apps if constantly high.

name: Idle
functionality: Not a real program — high values mean the CPU is free.

name: smss.exe
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.

name: csrss.exe
description: Handles console windows and parts of the Win32 subsystem.
functionality: Handles console windows and parts of the Win32 subsystem.
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.
A csrss.exe outside System32 is a strong indicator of malware masquerading as Windows.

name: wininit.exe
description: Starts services.exe and lsass.exe at boot.
functionality: Starts services.exe and lsass.exe at boot.
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.

name: winlogon.exe
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.

name: services.exe
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.

name: lsass.exe
description: Validates sign-ins and enforces security policy.
functionality: Validates sign-ins and enforces security policy.
troubleshooting: Core Windows process. Ending it crashes Windows, signs the user out, or is blocked by Windows.
High CPU can indicate many authentication requests (e.g. a misbehaving app or network scan).

name: LsaIso.exe
description: Isolated LSA process used by Credential Guard.
functionality: Isolated LSA process used by Credential Guard.

name: svchost.exe
description: Hosts Windows services. There are always many instances.
functionality: Each instance runs one or more services; the Services column shows which.
troubleshooting: Find which service is busy in the 'Services' column and look that service up.
Windows Update (wuauserv), Defender, and Delivery Optimization are common temporary CPU users.
svchost.exe anywhere other than System32/SysWOW64 should be investigated.
highCpu: One of its hosted services is busy — commonly Windows Update, Delivery Optimization, or Windows Search.

name: dwm.exe
description: Composes the desktop and window effects using the GPU.
functionality: Composes the desktop and window effects using the GPU.
troubleshooting: High GPU/CPU use often follows GPU driver problems or very high refresh/multiple monitors.
Update the GPU driver.
highMemory: Can grow with many monitors/high resolutions; a GPU driver leak can make it grow continuously — update the driver.

name: sihost.exe
description: Supports the Start menu, Action Center, and notifications.
functionality: Supports the Start menu, Action Center, and notifications.

name: explorer.exe
description: Taskbar, desktop, and File Explorer windows.
functionality: Taskbar, desktop, and File Explorer windows.
troubleshooting: If the taskbar freezes, restart Explorer from the console's Desktop actions.
High CPU usually comes from shell extensions (cloud sync overlays, archive tools) or a folder with thousands of thumbnails.
highCpu: Shell extensions, thumbnail generation, or a stuck network drive.

name: taskhostw.exe
description: Runs DLL-based scheduled and startup tasks.
functionality: Runs DLL-based scheduled and startup tasks.

name: RuntimeBroker.exe
troubleshooting: High usage is tied to a Store app (often Photos or Widgets) — close the related app.
highCpu: A Store app is busy (Photos indexing, Widgets, etc.).

name: dllhost.exe
description: Runs COM components such as thumbnail and media handlers.
functionality: Runs COM components such as thumbnail and media handlers.
highCpu: Usually thumbnail/codec handlers processing a large media folder.

name: ctfmon.exe
description: Text input services (keyboard layouts, IME, handwriting).
functionality: Text input services (keyboard layouts, IME, handwriting).

name: audiodg.exe
troubleshooting: High CPU usually comes from audio enhancements or vendor audio effects — disable enhancements for the device.
highCpu: Audio enhancements or a buggy audio driver effect.

name: spoolsv.exe
troubleshooting: High CPU or crashes are usually printer driver problems — restart the Print Spooler service and update/remove the printer driver.
highCpu: A stuck print job or bad printer driver.

name: WmiPrvSE.exe
troubleshooting: Constant high CPU means an app is querying WMI heavily — vendor utilities (RGB, hardware monitors) are common causes.
highCpu: Another app is polling system information (RGB/hardware monitoring tools, scripts).

name: WUDFHost.exe
description: Hosts user-mode drivers (sensors, fingerprint readers, MTP phones).
functionality: Hosts user-mode drivers (sensors, fingerprint readers, MTP phones).

name: SearchIndexer.exe
troubleshooting: High usage after copying many files is normal and temporary.
If constant, rebuild the index from Indexing Options.
highCpu: Indexing new or changed files; constant use suggests a corrupt index — rebuild it.

name: SearchFilterHost.exe
description: Extracts text from files for indexing.
functionality: Extracts text from files for indexing.

name: StartMenuExperienceHost.exe
troubleshooting: If Start won't open, ending this process restarts it.

name: ShellExperienceHost.exe
description: Notification area flyouts and system UI.
functionality: Notification area flyouts and system UI.

name: TextInputHost.exe
description: Touch keyboard, emoji panel, and IME UI.
functionality: Touch keyboard, emoji panel, and IME UI.

name: backgroundTaskHost.exe
description: Runs background tasks for Store apps.
functionality: Runs background tasks for Store apps.

name: smartscreen.exe
description: Checks downloaded files and apps against reputation data.
functionality: Checks downloaded files and apps against reputation data.

name: TiWorker.exe
troubleshooting: High CPU/disk is normal while updates install — let it finish and restart when asked.
highCpu: Installing or cleaning up updates. Normal for minutes to an hour after Patch Tuesday.

name: MoUsoCoreWorker.exe
description: Scans for and coordinates Windows updates.
functionality: Scans for and coordinates Windows updates.
troubleshooting: Often blocks sleep while checking for updates — check Windows Update status.
highCpu: Scanning for updates; temporary.

name: CompatTelRunner.exe
troubleshooting: Temporary high disk/CPU after updates; leave it to finish. The scheduled task can be reviewed in Settings Explorer → Scheduled tasks.
highCpu: Periodic compatibility scans; usually finishes within an hour.

name: Widgets.exe
startup: Runs while the Widgets button is enabled. Turn the button off in Taskbar settings to stop it.

name: PhoneExperienceHost.exe
startup: Starts at sign-in if Phone Link is set up; can be turned off inside Phone Link settings.

name: GameBarPresenceWriter.exe
description: Reports the running game to Xbox services.
functionality: Reports the running game to Xbox services.

name: msedge.exe
highMemory: Each tab and extension uses memory; use Edge's own task manager (Shift+Esc) to find heavy tabs.
startup: 'Startup boost' keeps Edge running after sign-in; can be turned off in edge://settings/system.

name: msedgewebview2.exe
description: Embedded browser engine used by many apps (Widgets, Teams, Outlook, games launchers).
functionality: Embedded browser engine used by many apps (Widgets, Teams, Outlook, games launchers).
troubleshooting: Memory belongs to the app that embeds it — check the parent process.
Never uninstall the WebView2 Runtime; many apps need it.

name: OneDrive.exe
highCpu: Syncing many files or stuck on a file — check the OneDrive icon for sync errors.
startup: Needed at startup for continuous backup of Desktop/Documents. Disable only if the customer doesn't use OneDrive.

name: SecurityHealthSystray.exe
startup: Keep enabled — it surfaces security warnings.

name: MsMpEng.exe
troubleshooting: High CPU during scheduled or first scans is normal.
Constant high CPU can come from scanning a folder that changes constantly (e.g. a game's shader cache, dev build folders) — review with the customer before adding exclusions.
highCpu: Scanning (scheduled scan, new downloads, or many changed files).

name: MRT.exe
highCpu: Monthly scan; finishes on its own.

name: wsappx
highCpu: Store app updates; temporary.

name: NVDisplay.Container.exe
description: Hosts NVIDIA Control Panel and display driver plugins.
functionality: Hosts NVIDIA Control Panel and display driver plugins.
troubleshooting: Required for NVIDIA Control Panel. If it uses high CPU, update or clean-install the driver.

name: nvcontainer.exe
highCpu: Overlay/recording features or driver update checks.

name: NVIDIA app.exe
description: Driver updates, game settings, and overlay.
functionality: Driver updates, game settings, and overlay.
startup: Not needed at startup unless the customer uses the overlay/recording; drivers still work without it.

name: NVIDIA Overlay.exe
description: In-game overlay, recording, and Instant Replay.
functionality: In-game overlay, recording, and Instant Replay.
troubleshooting: Instant Replay continuously records — turn it off if not used.

name: nvsphelper64.exe
description: Recording/hotkey helper for the NVIDIA overlay.
functionality: Recording/hotkey helper for the NVIDIA overlay.

name: RadeonSoftware.exe
description: AMD driver control panel and overlay.
functionality: AMD driver control panel and overlay.
startup: Needed for the AMD overlay/hotkeys and driver update notifications; graphics work without it.

name: AMDRSServ.exe
description: Background service for AMD Software features (ReLive, overlay).
functionality: Background service for AMD Software features (ReLive, overlay).

name: atieclxx.exe
description: Handles display hotkeys and events for the AMD driver.
functionality: Handles display hotkeys and events for the AMD driver.

name: igfxEM.exe
description: Intel graphics hotkeys and display events.
functionality: Intel graphics hotkeys and display events.

name: RtkAudUService64.exe
description: Realtek audio jack detection and audio console support.
functionality: Realtek audio jack detection and audio console support.
startup: Supports jack detection and the Realtek Audio Console — leave enabled.

name: WavesSvc64.exe
highCpu: Known to use CPU on some laptops; updating the audio driver from the laptop maker helps.

name: lghub.exe
startup: Needed at startup only for on-the-fly profile switching and lighting; onboard-memory profiles work without it.

name: Razer Synapse 3.exe
highCpu: Known to use CPU/memory; update Synapse or reinstall if constant.
startup: Needed at startup for lighting/macros not stored on the device.

name: iCUE.exe
description: Corsair RGB, fan, and peripheral control.
functionality: Corsair RGB, fan, and peripheral control.
highCpu: Lighting effects and hardware polling; reduce effect complexity or update iCUE.
startup: Controls fan curves on some systems — confirm before disabling at startup.

name: MSIAfterburner.exe
troubleshooting: If the PC is unstable, reset Afterburner to defaults — GPU overclocks are a common cause of crashes.

name: RTSS.exe
description: On-screen display and frame limiter used with Afterburner.
functionality: On-screen display and frame limiter used with Afterburner.
troubleshooting: Can conflict with other overlays and some anti-cheat systems.

name: ArmouryCrate.exe
description: ASUS RGB, fan, and system control.
functionality: ASUS RGB, fan, and system control.
highCpu: Lighting services are known to be heavy; update or use the official uninstall tool if not needed.

name: steam.exe
startup: Not needed at startup unless the customer wants downloads/updates in the background.

name: steamwebhelper.exe
highMemory: The Steam UI; disable GPU acceleration in Steam's Interface settings on low-end PCs.

name: EpicGamesLauncher.exe
highCpu: Known to use CPU while idle; close it after launching games.
startup: Not needed at startup.

name: Battle.net.exe
startup: Not needed at startup.

name: EADesktop.exe
startup: Not needed at startup.

name: upc.exe
startup: Not needed at startup.

name: RiotClientServices.exe
description: Launcher for Valorant and League of Legends.
functionality: Launcher for Valorant and League of Legends.

name: vgc.exe
troubleshooting: Requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on Windows 11.
Uninstall via Installed apps if the customer no longer plays Riot games.

name: EasyAntiCheat.exe
description: Anti-cheat service used by many games.
functionality: Anti-cheat service used by many games.
troubleshooting: Game won't launch: repair EAC from the game's install folder (EasyAntiCheat_Setup.exe).

name: BEService.exe
description: Anti-cheat service used by some games.
functionality: Anti-cheat service used by some games.

name: Overwolf.exe
highMemory: Each Overwolf app is a browser process; uninstall unused apps inside Overwolf.
startup: Not needed at startup; also bundled by CurseForge.

name: Discord.exe
troubleshooting: Black screen/glitches: toggle Hardware Acceleration, then clear the cache.
highCpu: Hardware acceleration issues or streaming; try toggling hardware acceleration in Discord settings.
highMemory: Electron app; several processes are normal.
startup: Optional at startup — users who want instant notifications keep it; it can start minimised.

name: Spotify.exe
startup: Not needed at startup; turn off in Spotify → Settings → Startup and window behaviour.

name: Teams.exe
highMemory: Large meetings and many chats use significant memory.
startup: Workplace users usually keep it at startup.

name: Zoom.exe
startup: Not needed at startup unless the customer joins many meetings.

name: obs64.exe
highCpu: Software (x264) encoding; switch to the GPU encoder (NVENC/AMF/QSV) in Output settings.

name: chrome.exe
highCpu: A busy tab or extension; check Chrome's Task Manager.
highMemory: Each tab/extension is a process; use Chrome's Task Manager (Shift+Esc) to find heavy tabs and extensions.
startup: 'Continue running background apps when Chrome is closed' keeps it in memory; can be turned off in chrome://settings/system.

name: firefox.exe
highMemory: Use about:processes to find heavy tabs.

name: opera.exe
startup: Opera installs a 'browser assistant' startup entry and auto-update tasks that can be disabled.

name: Dropbox.exe
startup: Needed at startup for continuous sync.

name: OfficeClickToRun.exe
description: Office updates and streaming installation service.
functionality: Office updates and streaming installation service.
troubleshooting: Office repair (Quick/Online) is started from Installed apps → Microsoft 365 → Modify.

name: OUTLOOK.EXE
highCpu: Large mailboxes indexing or a bad add-in; start with 'outlook.exe /safe' to test add-ins.

name: Creative Cloud.exe
startup: Not needed at startup unless the customer syncs Adobe fonts/files continuously.

name: GoogleUpdate.exe
startup: Runs via scheduled tasks; leave enabled so Chrome stays patched.

name: MicrosoftEdgeUpdate.exe
startup: Leave enabled — WebView2 security updates depend on it.

name: jusched.exe
startup: Old Java runtimes are a security risk — uninstall Java if no app needs it.

name: CCleaner64.exe
startup: 'Smart Cleaning' monitoring is not needed at startup. Avoid its registry cleaner on customer PCs.

name: wallpaper64.exe
highCpu: Animated wallpapers use GPU/CPU; set it to pause while games run.

name: MBAMService.exe
troubleshooting: Running alongside another real-time antivirus can slow the PC; keep one real-time product.

name: AvastSvc.exe
troubleshooting: Use the official avastclear tool for complete removal.

name: mcshield.exe
troubleshooting: Often pre-installed as a trial; remove with the McAfee Consumer Product Removal tool if the customer doesn't subscribe.

name: NortonSecurity.exe
troubleshooting: Remove with the Norton Remove and Reinstall tool.
